channel.title: Said & Checked: Defense and National Security — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day about Defense and National Security, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, Defense and National Security, 2026-11-25: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Jamie Raskin, Mike Rounds)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Jamie Raskin, U.S. Representative: “Reported as: Hadrian Automation, he wrote, received nearly $1 billion in U.S. Navy and Army contracts in March — its first-ever federal contracts — after bringing 1789 Capital on as an investor in 2025.” Unsettled. AskAmerica's federal contract records show one Hadrian award, from the Army in March 2026 ($39.2 million obligated on March 17, about $79.4 million in total by July), and no earlier federal contracts, which fits "first-ever." A Navy contract of about $900 million is reported only in trade press and no award record for it was found, and 1789 Capital's 2025 investment rests on secondary investor lists.
  • Mike Rounds, U.S. Senator: “Reported as: The criticism follows a classified directive from Hegseth that Republican U.S. Sen. Mike Rounds said largely restricts U.S. military officials' participation in Canadian think tank and social events.” Unsettled. As reported by Breaking Defense, Rounds said the memo requires permission for Canadian think tank events and social engagements and limits general and flag officer meetings to those that advance Defense Department objectives. The directive is classified and no Defense Department or Rounds-published account of its scope could be read, so whether it "largely restricts" participation is not settled.

item.title: Said & Checked, Defense and National Security, 2026-11-23: none false or contradicted, 1 unsupported (John Kennedy)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported

  • John Kennedy, U.S. Senator from Louisiana: “I have tried and failed, for 16 months, to convince Senator Thune, who has total control of the Senate and my Senate colleagues, to do that.” Unsupported. No record of a 16-month effort by Kennedy to add defense money to a reconciliation bill was found beyond his own remarks; the documented dispute is the November 2026 push for a $350 billion defense reconciliation package, which Senate Republicans paused on Nov. 19. The search covered news reports and the Meet the Press transcript, not Kennedy's press releases or the Congressional Record.

item.title: Said & Checked, Defense and National Security, 2026-11-20: none false or contradicted, 3 unsupported, 11 unsettled (Donald Trump, Deb Fischer)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “Reported as: They also agree that Iran cannot obtain a nuclear weapon, Trump said.” Unsupported. No Chinese record found says China agrees Iran cannot obtain a nuclear weapon. China's summit readout and the joint declaration speak of preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons in general and do not name Iran. Searched: the two Chinese Foreign Ministry readouts of Nov. 19, the joint declaration and AP's report; Xinhua could not be loaded, and no Chinese-language record was searched.
  • Deb Fischer, U.S. Senator: “the managers' package alone included amendments from Members on both sides of the aisle--38 from Republicans, 38 from Democrats--and 10 that were crafted on a bipartisan basis.” Unsupported. No published count of the managers' package amendments by party was found; the search covered the warehouse bill records and web searches, and no committee description of the package was located.
  • Deb Fischer, U.S. Senator: “our portion of this year's NDAA addressed 184 requests from Senators on both sides of the aisle.” Unsupported. No committee or subcommittee document stating 184 Senator requests was found; the search covered the warehouse and web searches.

item.title: Said & Checked, Defense and National Security, 2026-11-19: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Marco Rubio)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Marco Rubio, Secretary of State: “Reported as: Rubio told reporters there was "zero" evidence that the outages were connected or were tied to rival nations, cyber hackers or criminals.” Unsettled. The accounts found for each outage are non-malicious and none links them: Microsoft cites a latent software defect, JPMorgan Chase "a software bug" that "is not cyber-related," the NSA "temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance," and the FAA network data flooding. The NSA gave no further cause, the FAA account was not read from its primary document in this check, and Microsoft's final report was still pending, so the evidence does not fully decide the claim.

item.title: Said & Checked, Defense and National Security, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 1 unsupported, 1 unsettled (Mark Kelly, Markwayne Mullin)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • Mark Kelly, U.S. Senator from Arizona: “One parent told us that there's their kid, lost more than 45 pounds in six months because of a lack of food” Unsupported. Military.com's hearing report confirms Kelly said at the Nov. 17 hearing that a parent reported a child losing more than 45 pounds in six months. Searched: the AskAmerica catalog (no table covers it), Military.com, the PBS and Yahoo copies of the live blog, and an NPR interview from August 2026 in which Kelly described a different case (a grandmother, 20 to 25 pounds); no hearing transcript, press release or published report of the parent's account itself was found.
  • Markwayne Mullin, Secretary of Homeland Security: “Reported as: Mullin said the UK doesn't have the same safeguards and emergency preparedness the U.S has.” Unsettled. No common measure ranks U.S. and U.K. emergency preparedness; the warehouse holds U.S.-only FEMA tables and no U.K. data. The one comparable measure found, household-supply advice, exists in both countries (U.K. 72 hours; Ready.gov 'several days'). The U.K. government page was not read.
